# About
 
I started as a math major at UNL, but kept finding myself drawn to the messier, real world side of problems where the data is imperfect and the answer actually matters to someone. That's what pulled me toward data science.
 
Most of my experience has been in data validation and analysis. I built SQL workflows at a Berkshire Hathaway insurance company, managed course evaluation datasets for UNL, and modeled health outcomes at the census tract level using socioeconomic and geographic data. I like work that combines careful methodology and practical impact.
 
Lately I've been getting more interested in bioinformatics. Applying ML and statistical modeling to biological data feels like a natural extension of the kind of work I already do, and it's a space where rigor really matters. I don't have a deep biology background yet, but working alongside biology and bioinformatics majors and completing a hands on entomology lab has pushed me in that direction.
 
Outside of work, I spent a semester studying in Nishinomiya, Japan, and I'm a few years into studying Japanese, mostly for personal reasons, though I suspect it'll come in handy eventually.
 
I'm currently looking for data science or analyst roles, with a particular interest in biotech, health, or research adjacent environments.
